author: desk
note: Desk-written plain-English summary, not a tiered fact. Written to help a reader understand the business quickly; verify any figure against the fact store before using it in a report.
one_liner: A medical search tool that answers doctors' clinical questions with citations.
what_it_does: OpenEvidence answers clinical questions for practising doctors, drawing on peer-reviewed medical literature and citing what it used. It is free to verified clinicians and has spread rapidly through American medicine by word of mouth.
how_it_makes_money: Advertising to a highly valuable professional audience, rather than charging the doctors who use it.
why_it_matters: It is the clearest example of AI succeeding by going narrow and deep in one profession instead of competing as a general assistant.
competitive_position: Competes with established clinical reference tools, which charge subscriptions, and with general assistants, which are not trusted for clinical use.
key_risks: An advertising model inside clinical decision-making invites scrutiny about influence.
Medical liability if an answer contributes to a bad outcome.
Regulators may classify clinical decision support more strictly.
Incumbent reference providers have deep hospital relationships.

glossary.definition: Tools that help a clinician decide on diagnosis or treatment. A regulated category in many countries.
Research vetted by independent experts in the field before publication.
